item.title: How data centres affect electricity prices and for whom — CEPR / VoxEU
item.description:
Editor's note — September 24: This week is about transition costs and institutional adaptation: who pays when AI loads the grid, when supply chains are de-risked, when labor rules cross borders, and when institutions built for an earlier era meet new geopolitical and technological constraints.

CEPR / VoxEU · September 24, 2026 · ~9 min · Directly readable

Cameron Scalera, Valentina Bosetti and Filippo Pecci use U.S. utility-territory data to estimate how the post-2021 data-centre boom affects retail electricity prices. Their causal design finds that new facilities raise peak demand and grid spending, with residential customers bearing larger price increases than commercial or industrial users; the household effect is close to zero under nonprofit utilities. The policy implication is less “block data centres” than “decide who pays”: add generation and transmission, reward flexible loads, and use large-load tariffs to keep grid-upgrade costs from being socialized onto households.

Why it broadens: Turns the AI-infrastructure debate from megawatts and investment headlines into political economy: benefits are diffuse or concentrated elsewhere, while local ratepayers can absorb visible costs.

item.title: 獨家》巨大賠1億還不夠？美國海關暫扣令一週年，接下來還有歐盟？ — 天下雜誌
item.description:
天下雜誌 CommonWealth · 2026年9月23日 · 約12分鐘 · 文章頁可直接讀取

一年前，美國CBP以強迫勞動疑慮對巨大台灣廠自行車與零件發布暫扣令；受影響業務約占集團營收4至5%。一年來，巨大退還移工仲介費與相關費用約新台幣1億元、擴大零招聘費政策、改善宿舍並向美方提交整改資料；更重要的是，事件促使台灣自行車業啟動產業級人權盡職調查與第三方申訴機制。壓力也不只來自美國：歐盟禁止強迫勞動產品規則將於2027年12月開始適用。

Why it broadens: 把「供應鏈安全」從關稅、晶片與地緣政治拉到勞動制度。市場准入正在把移工招募、住宿、申訴與仲介費，變成製造業競爭力與治理能力的一部分。

item.title: How exchange rate policy reshapes global supply chains and productivity growth — CEPR / VoxEU
item.description:
CEPR / VoxEU · September 17, 2026 · ~9 min · Directly readable

Paul Bergin, Woo Jin Choi and Ju Hyun Pyun argue that persistent currency undervaluation, when sustained by reserve accumulation and capital controls, can do more than shift trade balances temporarily. Evidence from 45 countries associates the policy mix with greater manufacturing employment, firm entry and domestic sourcing of intermediate inputs. Their model adds firm dynamics and trade hysteresis: exchange-rate policy can induce entry at home and exit abroad, leaving a durable change in where production networks live even after the original price incentive fades.

Why it broadens: Challenges the clean separation between “macro” exchange-rate policy and “micro” industrial policy. Relative prices can become structural policy when they alter which firms and supplier networks survive.
